messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the hospital complaining of fever and cough over the last few days. The clinical evaluation revealed micro nodular shadowing consistent with miliary TB, which was confirmed through chest computed tomography. Broncho-alveolar lavage fluid was negative for acid-fast bacilli, but M. tuberculosis was identified through culture. Cerebrospinal fluid examination led to the diagnosis of probable TB meningitis. The patient developed a right side stroke and was subsequently transferred to a different hospital where the prescribed treatments and rehabilitation were continued. The patient continued with anti-TB, anti-HIV, and aspirin treatments leading to improvement in general and neurologic conditions. After five weeks, the patient was discharged.

Discharge Instructions:
The patient was discharged with follow-up appointments scheduled with the infectious disease clinic and neurological department. The patient was advised to continue with anti-TB, anti-HIV, and aspirin treatments as prescribed by the physician. The patient was also advised to maintain a healthy diet and lifestyle, quit smoking, take prescribed medications as directed, and avoid alcohol and recreational drugs. The patient is advised to seek medical attention immediately if any new symptoms or complications arise.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is miliary tuberculosis, confirmed by M. tuberculosis culture, with probable TB meningitis and a stroke as complications. This sits in chapter A, category A19. HIV is implied by the anti-HIV treatment, and Australian HIV coding rules could make B24 the principal diagnosis instead, but HIV is not documented as a diagnosis here.

CODE: A19
